clue.text: New limo to be given gold front — special example of this!

definitions.text: New limo to be given gold front — special example of this!

indicators.note: the gold is placed at the front, ahead of the other letters

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: new here signals the words are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A brand-new limousine gets a gilded front end, a showpiece of the motor trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' is the anagram signal and 'front' places the gold first. The whole clue doubles as definition: a gold-trimmed limo is one special instance of the general vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A limousine is one particular kind of motor car, so a fancy limo is a special example of the general vehicle.

clue.text: Star taken round hospital, being hurt

indicators.note: the word for star is wrapped round the hospital letter

parts.note: an ace is a star performer
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A celebrity is rushed round to hospital after an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel hurt and to feel pain are the same sensation; the verb is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Pig out getting this food?

parts.note: pigs are sent out to sniff for this underground fungus; 'pig out' also means to overeat

explanation.surface: Someone gorging on a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pig out' looks like greedy eating, but read literally it is a pig sent out foraging, as truffle hunters use.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs have long been used to root out the prized edible underground fungus.

clue.text: Women at matches taking a leading role?

definitions.text: Women at matches taking a leading role?

parts.words: Women at matches taking a leading role?
parts.note: matches are weddings here, and the chief bridesmaids lead the bride's attendants

explanation.surface: Female footballers or players captaining their side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' suggests sport, but a match is also a marriage; the chief attendants of a bride lead the others.
explanation.definitionFit: At a wedding the principal bridesmaids head the bridal party, so they take the leading role among the women.

clue.text: Rough sound with one drunk turning up for Mexican food

parts.note: a burr is a rough rolling sound, as of a whirring machine or a rolled R
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for drunk is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard

explanation.surface: A drunk staggers in, growling, to order Mexican food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses SOT to give TOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortillas wrapped round a filling are a staple dish of Mexican cooking.

clue.text: Not up for deceitful action

definitions.meaning: still ... down, in bed rather than risen

explanation.surface: Someone stays in bed to dodge a dishonest scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prone in bed and telling falsehoods share one word, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Old boy may be given it — but not while still alive!

definitions.text: Old boy may be given it — but not while still alive!

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil receives an honour that only comes after death.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a death notice is something a former pupil may get in the school magazine, but only once dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A death notice in a newspaper or magazine is printed only after someone has died.

clue.text: Indicate something risky — zero range of knowledge!

parts.note: a bet is a gamble, a risk
O looks like the figure zero
ken is one's range of knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: A warning that knowing nothing is a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: To be a sign or omen of something is to signal it, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Like violent 10, changing terrain to lake?

indicators.note: changing signals that the letters of the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A flood turns the land into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' is the anagram signal. 10 refers to 10-across, the clue about rain, so 'violent 10' is a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: Pouring, violent rain is described as falling in torrents, the adjective for a downpour.

clue.text: Sixty minutes with one alluring female

parts.note: an hour is sixty minutes
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A quick hour with a seductive woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition, a beautiful maiden of paradise; by extension any seductive woman.

clue.text: Crumbling terrain around Western Australia — does it need this?

definitions.text: Crumbling terrain around Western Australia — does it need this?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the state's abbreviation
crumbling land breaks up, so the letters break up and re-form

parts.note: WA is the abbreviation for the Australian state

explanation.surface: Drought-cracked land in the Australian outback, crying out for a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumbling' rearranges the land to RAINTER, which 'around' wraps about the state. The whole clue also defines: parched crumbling soil needs a soaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched, crumbling ground in a dry state needs water from the sky to bind it.

clue.text: Hit by hostile elements

parts.note: elements are wind, rain and storm, which batter and wear things down

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hostile elements' sounds like an enemy force, but the elements are the forces of nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn and battered by wind and rain over time has been struck by the forces of nature.

clue.text: Rod may go along with me to the river

definitions.text: Rod may go along with me to the river

parts.words: Rod may go along with me to the river
parts.note: the speaker is the angler's gear: line, hooks and reel accompany the rod

explanation.surface: Someone called Rod tags along on a riverside walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name, but it is a fishing rod, and 'me' is the rest of the angling kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's equipment, the hooks, lines and reels, travels with the rod to the water.

clue.text: Inclined to give a special emphasis

definitions.text: Inclined to give a special emphasis

parts.words: Inclined to give a special emphasis
parts.note: slanted type is used to stress words in print

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined to' reads as 'tending to', but it means literally sloped, as slanting print is.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers set words in sloping type to stress them, so the letters lean for emphasis.

clue.text: Go right back around rocks to find amphibian

indicators.note: the reversed letters sit around the word for rocks
back means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written
a reef is a ridge of rocks in the sea

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn back past some rocks to spot a frog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is taken literally, not as a verb of motion; 'back' reverses it with the abbreviation for right, making TROG, a word that then wraps around the rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: This climbing frog is one kind of amphibian, an animal living on land and in water.

clue.text: Part of county in south-east — it's not this around north-east!

indicators.note: the word goes around the compass letters

parts.note: not this one but that one
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: A puzzled note that a place in south-east England is not in the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: The district is in Kent, the county at England's south-eastern tip. 'it's not this' gives THAT, the other demonstrative.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Thanet is a district at the north-eastern corner of Kent, a county in south-east England.

clue.text: Store's top jumpers? They may be looking for them

definitions.text: They may be looking for them

indicators.note: top means the first letter of the word, as this is a down clue

parts.note: hoppers are things that jump

explanation.surface: A department store's best-selling sweaters, sought after by customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' in the surface are sweaters (British for pullovers), and in the definition 'them' refers to those sweaters that customers hunt for.
explanation.definitionFit: Customers in a store are the people browsing for pullovers to buy.

clue.text: Skin preparation? Simpleton absorbs it the wrong way

indicators.note: the word for simpleton takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a loon is a fool or simpleton

indicators.note: the wrong way means the word it is turned backwards

explanation.surface: A fool soaks up a skin cream by applying it badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Simpleton' is the container, not the definition; 'the wrong way' turns the little word round to give TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream or liquid rubbed on the skin is a cosmetic or medicinal preparation.

clue.text: This Rev. spouting does well

indicators.note: a vicar spouting pours words out in a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clergyman preaching at length is doing very nicely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spouting' rearranges the letters of THIS REV.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or prosper is to do well, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Personal appeal of woman who does and is attached to mum

indicators.note: attached to means the next letters follow on

parts.note: a char, short for charwoman, is a cleaning lady, a 'woman who does' in British idiom
Ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: The magnetism of a cleaner who is devoted to her mother.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHAR is a British cleaning woman, and 'a woman who does' is the old phrase for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic charm that draws people to someone is their personal appeal.

clue.text: Little girl has point to make about a particular pope

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a little girl in the family
a tine is a point or prong, as of a fork

explanation.surface: A young girl makes a point about a pope.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to Pope Sixtus, as in the chapel he built in the Vatican.

clue.text: They may need to get the political landscape mapped out afresh

definitions.text: They may need to get the political landscape mapped out afresh

parts.words: They may need to get the political landscape mapped out afresh
parts.note: when borders change, map-makers must redraw them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Political landscape' sounds like the state of politics, but here it is the literal map of countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Map-makers redraw political maps when frontiers move after wars or treaties.

clue.text: Indian female managed to keep English in tow repeatedly

indicators.note: in tow means the next letters are trailed behind

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

indicators.note: repeatedly means the letter appears twice

explanation.surface: An Indian woman keeps the English along behind her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles E, and 'in tow' puts EE behind RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu queen or a rajah's wife; the title is used for Indian royal women.

clue.text: Request around start of recital for a particular composer

indicators.note: the word for request goes around the letter

parts.note: to beg is to request

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An appeal for a recital of a favourite composer's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School, one particular composer.

clue.text: A new Conservative in very bad breakaway movement

indicators.note: the letters are placed inside the word for very bad

parts.note: severe means very bad, as in a severe storm
C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British party

explanation.surface: A newly elected Tory joins a disastrous breakaway faction.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting ties and breaking away from a group is a separation or split.

clue.text: Rubbish food from the butcher?

definitions.meaning: cow's stomach lining, sold by butchers

explanation.surface: Someone sneering at a butcher's offal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both worthless nonsense and the edible stomach lining of cattle.

clue.text: Mark's violent movement

definitions.meaning: a short horizontal line used as punctuation
a sudden rush or hurried run

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark makes a sudden lunge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a punctuation stroke and a sudden headlong rush.

clue.text: Physicist of principle begins here to be disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A principled scientist says his work starts here and he will not be interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be disturbed' rearranges BEGINS HERE; 'of principle' points to the uncertainty principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Werner Heisenberg formulated the uncertainty principle of quantum mechanics.
